grammar.title: Frase
grammar.rule: É uma hora. São duas horas e meia. Primeiro os livros, depois as cadeiras.

rows: às duas horas e meia da tarde
de manhã / à tarde / à noite

grammar.note_en:
Clock time is the new grammatical target. Hora means “hour”; hours is horas. At the current café moment, É uma hora means “It is one o’clock.” Use singular é with uma hora and plural são with more than one: São duas horas e meia means “It is half past two.” These statements tell the time; they do not say when an action happens. The dialogue and diagrams introduce the actual forms before practice. The pronoun it in English has no separate Portuguese word in these clock statements.

To say when an action takes place, put à before the singular uma hora and às before a plural hour expression. Os livros chegam à uma hora means “The books arrive at one o’clock”; As cadeiras chegam às duas horas e meia means “The chairs arrive at half past two.” The marks on à and às distinguish these time prepositions from the articles a/as. Keep the singular/plural distinction: à uma hora, “at one o’clock”; às duas horas, “at two o’clock”; às nove horas, “at nine o’clock.” The chapter uses this bounded clock-time convention; it does not teach every use of à or all alternative editorial treatments of uma.

The clock reference relates 13:00 to uma hora da tarde (“one o’clock in the afternoon”) and 14:30 to duas horas e meia da tarde (“half past two in the afternoon”). The digits are written clock records, not an instruction to invent number words above twenty. Meia here means half of an hour. It is feminine, matching hora; do not change it to meio after a masculine number. Duas horas e meia is two full hours plus half an hour, not two and a half chairs. We do not introduce minute counting or a full set of half expressions. The table contains only expressions actually used in the story.

Distinguish de manhã, à tarde and à noite: these mean “in the morning,” “in the afternoon” and “at night.” To identify which part of the day a particular hour belongs to, the story uses da manhã or da tarde: nove horas da manhã means “nine o’clock in the morning”; uma hora da tarde means “one o’clock in the afternoon.” Às oito horas da noite means “at eight o’clock at night.” Da is the familiar contraction de + a. No sábado means “on Saturday”; no domingo means “on Sunday.” These are particular days in this schedule. The chapter does not teach a claim about habitual Saturdays or Sundays.

Hoje means “today,” ontem “yesterday,” and amanhã “tomorrow.” The calendar attaches these words to the current Friday and places sábado (“Saturday”) immediately after it, then domingo (“Sunday”). A day word does not itself create a past or future tense. No papel de ontem não tem os dois nomes means “On yesterday’s sheet there are not the two names”: this describes the sheet visible now, without requiring a past verb. Amanhã é sábado means “Tomorrow is Saturday.” Domingo, os livros voltam ao mercado means “On Sunday the books return to the market”: the present verb is used for an agreed schedule. It does not introduce ir + infinitive. In Vou ao café com os livros (“I go to the café with the books”), vou still expresses movement to a place.

Antes means “before” and depois “after.” Primeiro os livros, depois as cadeiras means “First the books, then the chairs.” Antes das duas horas e meia means “before half past two”; depois das duas horas e meia, “after half past two.” The familiar de + as contraction gives das. Cedo means “early”: Às nove horas é cedo means “Nine o’clock is early.” Early is relative to the person’s work here, not a grammatical label for every morning time.

Primeiro/primeira and segundo/segunda express first and second. O primeiro nome means “the first name”; a primeira pessoa, “the first person”; o segundo nome, “the second name”; a segunda pessoa, “the second person.” The ending agrees with the noun. In Primeiro os livros (“First the books”), primeiro orders actions; it does not agree with livros. The chapter does not require unseen ordinal numbers. The two separate contacts confirm the entire revised schedule. An entry in Rosa’s notebook is not evidence that a contact has heard or accepted it. The weather hook uses the delivered phone drawing with the already taught tomorrow/night labels; no weather noun, weather verb, future periphrasis or conditional is introduced.
